title: Variable-width vector adapter + staged reindex for rerank endpoints
creator: Maya Chen
body:
Problem: We have an increasing number of models producing embeddings at different vector widths (e.g., 256, 512, 1024) for specialized reranking and semantic search workloads. Current index topology assumes a single fixed width per index and our clients assume width stability. Changing width requires full reindexing and client updates, which causes long maintenance windows and potential client mismatches. Goal: allow the reranking endpoint and embedding pipeline to tolerate mixed-width vectors during a migration with minimal client changes and without a global downtime reindex.

Proposal summary: build a lightweight "variable-width adapter" layer in the indexer/service mesh + a staged shard reindex strategy that: (1) lets the query path accept queries and candidate vectors of differing widths, (2) uses a small learned linear projection + fallback asymmetric similarity path to compare different widths, (3) ships a client-SDK handshake and header to surface index vector_width and compatibility, and (4) migrates shards progressively with per-shard feature flags and telemetry-driven gating.

Key design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Projection vs. multiple indexes: We prefer a projection approach (learned linear mapper per width pair) because it avoids duplicating indexes and reduces storage cost. Tradeoff: potential quality regression if projection is imperfect. Mitigation: keep fallback rerank flow using original high-dim vectors when possible and run A/B evals.
- Learned projection type: use a small dense linear layer (no non-linearity) trained offline on aligned embedding pairs from source and target models. Store per-shard projection metadata; keep projection inference on CPU with optimized BLAS for minimal memory.
- Asymmetric fallback path: if projection confidence < threshold, compute asymmetric similarity using raw vectors + cross-encoder rerank for top-K (K=50). This increases latency for a small fraction of queries but preserves quality.
- Client SDK handshake: SDKs will fetch index metadata (index_info) that includes supported_widths and recommended_client_width; queries include header X-Embed-Width to allow server to choose projection path. Backwards-compatible: if client doesn't send header, assume default width matching most shards.

Migration plan (staged):
1) Build adapter and projection infra + offline training pipeline (2 weeks).
2) Canary: enable adapter on a single low-traffic tenant, run with projection on cold reads, collect quality metrics for 14 days (recall@10, MRR, delta from baseline).
3) Progressive shard enablement: enable per-shard flag to mark index as "support-multi-width". Reindex one shard at a time to new width while adapter remains active. Monitor recall vs. latency.
4) Client rollout: release SDK changes that include handshake and header support; keep header optional. Encourage customers to update but do not require immediately.
5) Full cutover: when 90% of traffic is handled by projection + fallback metrics are within thresholds, flip default recommended_client_width.
6) Cleanup: retire projection fallbacks after 3 full cycles with no regressions; remove per-shard flags.

Operational metrics and SLOs to monitor: 
- Rerank 50q latency P95 < 120ms (target); P99 < 250ms with fallback volume <= 2% of queries.
- Recall@10 relative delta vs. baseline <= 1.5% for canary traffic.
- Indexing throughput per-shard during reindexing: baseline +/- 10%.
- Error rate for projection path < 0.1%.

Testing plan: offline synthetic dataset with aligned pairs from both models for projection training and evaluation; A/B production cohorts; gold prompt evals and query logs replay; chaos tests for partial failure of projection service to validate fallback correctness.

Rollback triggers: sustained >3% recall degradation for 2h, or P99 rerank latency > 400ms for >30m, or fallback volume > 8% for >1h. On trigger: flip per-shard flags to prefer same-width-only flow and pause further reindexes.

Deliverables: 
- Projection training pipeline (data collection + trainer)
- Runtime adapter binary + per-shard projection metadata schema
- SDK handshake/header update + migration guide
- Runbook and dashboard (recall/latency/fallback ratio)

Links to specifications and artifacts are in `links` and `attachments`.

2026-02-24 - Diego Alvarez: Prototype complete (single CPU matrix multiply) — initial offline evaluation shows 0.9% averaged Recall@10 drop projecting 1024->512 on validation set. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/3221

2026-03-03 - Maya Chen: Ran canary data plan; legal asked about telemetry opt-out for PII-sensitive customers; added per-tenant opt-out flag for debug payloads in migration guide.

2026-03-08 - Diego Alvarez: Load test results uploaded: projection path adds ~6ms median latency, top-K fallback triggered for ~0.9% of queries. P95 increase within target. Link: https://perf.redwood/bench/ENG-74321
